# entire-graph — instructions for coding agents (follow directly)

You have a deterministic local code graph: `entire graph` (functions, classes, methods,
types, routes + call/inheritance relations; no network). These instructions are FOR YOU, the
agent reading this file. Use the graph to narrow exploration without trading away correctness.

## The workflow (mandatory for locate/fix/change tasks)

Your FIRST action on any task that requires finding code must be ONE search:

    entire graph search --repo . --profile full --query "<the task or bug in one sentence>"

Then open the top hit's file with your file-read tool (pass a line range around the reported
line), inspect enough surrounding behavior to justify the change, and make the smallest complete
edit. Treat graph output as evidence, not an oracle.

## Hard rules

1. SEARCH FIRST — never grep/find/cat to locate code before you have searched.
2. READ focused source around the result. Widen the check when aliases, generated code, dynamic
   dispatch, or related implementations could matter.
3. Use graph follow-ups only when they answer a real question. For impact or callers, prefer:
       entire graph impact --repo . --symbol X
4. Make the smallest complete edit and check sibling sites or contracts when the task implies them.
5. VERIFY before stopping. Run the most focused relevant test, build, or reproduction available.
   If execution is unavailable, perform a bounded source-level verification and state the limit.
6. Prefer precise queries and line ranges, but never trade resolution for fewer turns.
7. Feature-detect before relying on semantic relations:
       entire graph capabilities --json

## When NOT to use the graph

If the task already names the exact file and it is small, just read it — the graph saves tokens
by eliminating exploration; when there is nothing to explore, skip it.

## Reference

    locate  ->  entire graph search --repo . --profile full --query "..."
    impact  ->  entire graph impact --repo . --symbol X   (one shot: callers, callees, type consumers, data flow, co-change, siblings)
    callers ->  entire graph neighbors --repo . --symbol X --relation CALLS --direction in

    stats   ->  entire graph stats --repo .        (human-facing token-savings report; not part of your workflow — do not run it unless asked)

# CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **AI Collaboration Rule**:
> - **Planning**, **Brainstorming**, **Implementation** and **Bug fixes** are all
>   in scope. Planning is no longer delegated to Gemini (Antigravity).
> - Implementation plans go in `.claude/plans/` (see
>   [rules/planning.md](rules/planning.md)); design decisions that outlive a plan
>   are recorded in `docs/backlog.md`. Open work (stories, tasks, bugs) is tracked
>   in Plane, see the `## Plane` section of the root `CLAUDE.md`.
> - Always refer to [project-context.md](../project-context.md) for global project rules.
>   It sits in this repository, at the root. The absolute path this line used to
>   carry named a GitLab checkout that is no longer where DevDesk lives.

## Project Overview

DevDesk is a terminal-based TUI (Text User Interface) application built with Go and Bubble Tea framework. It provides DevSecOps functionality including:
- System status monitoring (HTTP/HTTPS, ICMP, DNS, SSL checks)
- GitLab integration (authentication, project explorer, multi-select clone)
- Security scanning (Trivy CVE/secret/license/misconfig + Gitleaks secrets)
- Container management with real-time metrics, on Docker or Podman (`app.container_engine`)
- OCI resource management (image scanning, container launching, network inspection)
- Network diagnostics (DNS, route, ICMP, TCP, TLS, HTTP) + real-time port monitoring + this machine's interfaces + local port forwarding (unprivileged, loopback only)
- Multi-context configuration management via YAML
- Local workspaces management with git metadata
- Claude Code session list (`:agent-usage` / `:au`): sessions found on this machine, by project and date, and per session the agent tree (orchestrator and sub-agents: types, models, tokens, share of the total; sortable by Total; also per agent a state (running / idle / done / unknown, idle after 5 min without a transcript line) shown as a status dot in the first column (the `running` dot blinks, DEVDESK-151) and as text, tool calls and duration; and an indicative cost per agent, `Est. cost` (orange from 75 % and red from 90 % of the session's estimated cost, when at least two agents are priced), from prices you write in the context YAML (`agent_usage.prices`, none shipped), with the session's `Billed` cost and `Unattributed` in the header, DEVDESK-47; a `Breakdown` colour bar per agent and, with `tab` inside a session, a Breakdown tab splitting the whole session's tokens by category, model and agent, as a percentage of tokens, DEVDESK-98). An open session updates live: read again every 2 s while active, only what was appended; paused after 5 min with no write and no unfinished sub-agent, or when its transcript is gone (header `Updates › paused`); `ctrl+r` reads it again in full. The sessions list itself is not live.

## Build and Development Commands

Tasks live in `mise.toml` — there is no Makefile. `mise tasks` lists them all.

```bash
# Development (fastest)
mise run dev          # Run directly with go run
go run .

# Build
mise run build        # Build binary to bin/dk
mise run run          # Build and run

# Testing
mise run test         # Run all tests
mise run cover        # Coverage per package
go test -v ./...      # Run all tests with verbose output
go test ./internal/command  # Run tests for specific package
mise run test-race    # Detect race conditions (critical for Bubble Tea Cmds)

# Code Quality
mise run fmt          # Format code
mise run vet          # Run go vet
mise run lint         # MANDATORY before commits - golangci-lint
mise run tidy         # Tidy dependencies
mise run check        # fmt + vet + lint + test in one go

# Installation
mise run install      # Install to $GOPATH/bin
```

`test-race` needs cgo and therefore a C compiler (`gcc`/`clang`) on `PATH`.

## Git, worktrees, pull requests — absolute rules

- Work happens in a worktree under `.worktrees/<branch>`, created from `origin/main`; the main checkout stays clean, on `main`.
- Never push directly to `main`: the Entire mirror rejects it, and so does the `main-protection` ruleset. Everything goes through a PR, merged once `Lint and build` and `Test` are green.
- Always use `gh -R anthnel/devdesk` (`origin` is `entire://`). There is one remote, `origin`; do not add a second one pointing at GitHub.
- A red `Entire Gates` check caused by Approvals alone does not block a merge (Findings, Checks, Up to date must stay green).
- In a sandbox, only commit; the host pushes, opens the PR and merges. Whoever creates a worktree removes it (never `git worktree prune` from the other side). The sandbox creates its own worktree; the host never creates one for it.
- Before creating a worktree or branch, pushing, opening/merging a PR or removing a worktree, load the `git-worktree-pr` skill.

## Releases

Only merging the release-please PR publishes a release; never merge it without the user's explicit agreement. After every merge on main, the orchestrating session loads the `release-flow` skill and checks the triggers.

## Architecture

The deep notes live in `docs/architecture/`, one file per area, and they are
**not** `@`-imported: an `@` would inline all of it into every session, which is
the thing this split exists to avoid. Read the file that covers what you are
touching, and update it in the same commit as the code.

| File | Covers |
|---|---|
| [`app-shell.md`](../docs/architecture/app-shell.md) | the router and its views, `ctrl+p` and the command parser, the keyboard vocabulary (`internal/ui/keymap`), greyed shortcuts, `shared.State`, cross-view messages, the jobs registry (`internal/jobs`), the one animation tick (blink phase, `app.motion`), the failure memory (`jobs.FailureKey`, `ChangedMsg.Failures`), the activity-column guard (`activity_guard_test.go`) and the `:jobs` view |
| [`configuration.md`](../docs/architecture/configuration.md) | the config schema, the contexts, the migrations (`gitlab:` → `forge:`, `docker:` → `network:`), `agent_usage.prices`, and the configuration view |
| [`forge.md`](../docs/architecture/forge.md) | `internal/forge` and its two backends, `forge.Vocabulary`, the explorer's clone pipeline, and how the explorer reads the forge index (`internal/forgeindex`) and its `g` |
| [`workspaces.md`](../docs/architecture/workspaces.md) | the `ws` file icons (`internal/ui/fileicon`) and the sync (`F`) |
| [`filebrowser.md`](../docs/architecture/filebrowser.md) | `:files` (`internal/ui/filebrowser`, `internal/fsbrowse`), the path picker a form's path field opens with enter, and `theme.ShortPath` |
| [`viewer.md`](../docs/architecture/viewer.md) | `internal/viewer` + `internal/ui/viewer` — kinds, displays, colouring, search, follow |
| [`scanning.md`](../docs/architecture/scanning.md) | Trivy, Gitleaks, plumber, `scan.Categorize`, the `:sec` inventory, the two scan caches, image signatures (`internal/trust`, the cosign verifier) |
| [`registries.md`](../docs/architecture/registries.md) | the registry/group model and the discovered-members cache |
| [`network.md`](../docs/architecture/network.md) | `internal/docker` and `internal/oci`, image updates (`internal/imageupdate`, the Update column), verified pulls (`internal/imagepull`), the netdiag view, `internal/ports`, `internal/netiface` |
| [`mcp.md`](../docs/architecture/mcp.md) | the MCP server the TUI serves over HTTP |
| [`templates.md`](../docs/architecture/templates.md) | `internal/template` + `internal/ui/templates` — the repository-template catalog, its three sources, how files are fetched, and the `:templates` view |
| [`ui-components.md`](../docs/architecture/ui-components.md) | `components.FooterMessage`, `internal/ui/datatable`, and the activity indicator column (`internal/ui/indicator`, `datatable.IndicatorColumn`, the row sentences `components.DescribeRow`) |
| [`agent-usage.md`](../docs/architecture/agent-usage.md) | `internal/agentusage` — per-agent token counts from Claude Code transcripts: format, aggregation rules, tolerance, privacy (`cwd` amendment), caps, ccusage cross-check; `ListSessions`; incremental reading (`ReadDelta`, `Aggregate`, `Activity.Settled`); tool calls and time span per agent (DEVDESK-46); per-model tokens, `Billed`, and the cost estimate (`internal/agentusage/pricing`, prices from `agent_usage.prices`, DEVDESK-47); the `:agent-usage` view and its agents level and State/Tools/Duration/Est. cost columns; the Breakdown column and tab, `Usage.Categories`/`ModelTotals` (DEVDESK-98) (`internal/ui/agentusageview`) |

### Status Monitoring System

**Factory Pattern for Checkers:**
- `internal/status/checker.go` - Main orchestrator
- `internal/status/http_checker.go` - HTTP/HTTPS checks
- `internal/status/icmp_checker.go` - ICMP ping checks
- `internal/status/dns_checker.go` - DNS resolution checks

Each checker implements `CheckerInterface`. The main `Checker.CheckOne()` uses a factory pattern to instantiate the right checker based on `component.Type`.

**Parallel Execution:**
- `CheckAll()` runs all component checks concurrently using goroutines and sync.WaitGroup
- Results are collected and returned as `[]ComponentStatus`

### Component CRUD Operations

Status view supports adding/editing/deleting monitors:
- `internal/ui/status/components/component_form.go` - Form component
- `internal/ui/status/components/confirm_modal.go` - Confirmation dialog
- Changes persist to `~/.devdesk/config.yaml` via `config.Save()`

State flags in Model: `creating`, `editing`, `confirming`, `selectedIdx`

### Credentials Management

No secret DevDesk holds is written to a file DevDesk owns. `internal/credentials`
implements the `Storage` interface three ways and `Select()` picks exactly one —
writing to several at once is what let the old "secure" option store a token in
the credential manager *and* in plaintext:

| Storage | Backend | Notes |
|---------|---------|-------|
| `KeyringStorage` | Windows Credential Manager / macOS Keychain / Secret Service | via `zalando/go-keyring`, no cgo. The default. |
| `GitCredentialStorage` | git's configured credential helper | Only when the helper is not `store`, which writes plaintext. Context-aware. |
| `MemoryStorage` | this process | Last resort, and deliberately worse: the auth view says nothing was saved. |

`Select(context, preference)` returns a `Selection{Storage, Backend, Detail}`.
The order is keyring → git credential → memory; `app.secret_backend` in the
context config pins the head of it (`auto`, `keyring`, `git-credential`). A
pinned backend that is unreachable falls through to memory rather than silently
to the other one.

The router resolves one `Selection` per context and keeps it in
`shared.State.Secrets`. It must be reused for the lifetime of the context — a
second `Select()` call yields a fresh `MemoryStorage` that cannot see what the
first one holds.

`MigrateLegacySecrets` runs at startup and on every context switch: a
`gitlab.token` or `registry.password` left in a context file by an older build
is moved into the store and deleted from the YAML, with the result reported in
the auth view.

## Testing

Test files follow Go conventions (`*_test.go`):
- `internal/command/parser_test.go` - Command parser tests
- `internal/app/app_test.go` - App router tests

Use table-driven tests where appropriate.

**`go test` does not detect races or explore fuzz targets.** `mise run test` runs
only the fuzz seeds, so `internal/agentusage` concurrency tests
(`TestConcurrent*`) need `mise run test-race`. To explore `FuzzIncrementalMatchesFull`
run `go test -fuzz=FuzzIncrementalMatchesFull -fuzztime=60s ./internal/agentusage`.

**HOME is shared across a test process.** `TestMain` in `internal/app` sets
`HOME` once for the whole process, so under `go test -count=N` a test finds
the files its own previous run wrote (context config, forge index cache), and
it fails from `-count=2` while `-count=1` passes (DEVDESK-36). A test that
writes under HOME isolates it with `t.Setenv("HOME", t.TempDir())` and
`USERPROFILE` too; in `internal/app`, call `isolateHome(t)` from
`harness_test.go` (already done by `routerAt`). `internal/ui/setup` is fixed
(DEVDESK-38): its `isolateHome(t)` helper in `model_test.go` is called by the
tests that write under HOME. Other packages whose TestMain does
`os.Setenv("HOME", …)` may have the same default. To find them:
`grep -rn 'os.Setenv("HOME"' --include=*_test.go`, then `go test -count=2` on each package.

**Never get a "free" port by `net.Listen("tcp", "127.0.0.1:0")`, reading the
port, then `Close()`, and letting the code under test bind it later.** Between
the close and the bind, any `bind(0)` can be handed that very port: an
`httptest.NewServer` in the same test, another test, another process on the
runner. The symptom is an intermittent `address already in use`, mostly in CI
(Linux gave the just-closed port back to about 1 `bind(0)` in 7,000; DEVDESK-35,
D85 in `docs/backlog.md`).

- If the code under test takes a port, call `loopback.ReservePort(t)`
  (`internal/testutil/loopback`). On Linux it holds a socket bound with
  `SO_REUSEADDR`, never listening, until `t.Cleanup`: `bind(0)` and `connect()`
  cannot take the port, but `net.Listen` can.
- Otherwise let the server bind `:0` and read the real port, or keep the
  listener open and hand it to the code under test.
- Off Linux, `ReservePort` keeps the old behavior and the window stays open
  (on Windows Go does not set `SO_REUSEADDR`). That is known, not a local bug.
- `internal/testutil/loopback` is imported from `_test.go` files only; nothing
  enforces it yet.

**Test input and colour (DEVDESK-199).** Build keys only through
`internal/ui/testutil` (`Key`, `Keys`, `Type`, `Paste`, `Text`, `IsText`), never a
literal `tea.KeyMsg` or `tea.Key*`. `Key` is strict: an unknown name panics. The
space key is built as a key (`KeySpace` + rune `' '`), never matched through
`String()` (v1 `" "`, v2 `"space"`). The colour profile is forced through
`internal/testutil/colorprofile` (`TrueColor(t)`, `Force()` in `TestMain`), the only
importer of termenv; it is a leaf package because testutil→shortcut→theme would
cycle. `internal/ui/testutil/source_guard_test.go` fails the suite on a hand-built
key, a termenv import or `SetColorProfile` in any `_test.go`. Paste tests
(`internal/app/paste_test.go`, `wrapped_input_test.go`, `component_form_test.go`):
a paste reaches the focused field, newlines become spaces in single-line fields,
and no key action fires (Rule 111).

**Space and key API (DEVDESK-200).** Production code matches the space key as
`keymap.Space`, never `" "`/`"space"`, and reads keys through `String()` only
(no `.Runes`, `.Alt`, `.Paste`, `tea.KeyType` or `tea.Key<Name>`). Two guards in
`internal/ui/keymap` (`space_scan_test.go`, `legacy_key_scan_test.go`) fail the
suite otherwise; limits are listed in `docs/architecture/app-shell.md`.

## Dependencies

Key libraries (see `go.mod`):
- `github.com/charmbracelet/bubbletea` - TUI framework
- `github.com/charmbracelet/bubbles` - Pre-built TUI components (table, textinput, spinner)
- `github.com/charmbracelet/lipgloss` - Styling
- `gitlab.com/gitlab-org/api/client-go` - GitLab API client
- `github.com/prometheus-community/pro-bing` - ICMP ping functionality (maintained fork of go-ping/ping)
- `github.com/google/go-github/v68` - GitHub API client (§3.6)
- `github.com/libp2p/go-netroute` - which interface a destination leaves by, on all three platforms (§3.44)
- `github.com/zalando/go-keyring` - host secret manager (wincred / Keychain / Secret Service), no cgo
- `gopkg.in/yaml.v3` - YAML configuration

## Code Conventions

- Comments: **English only** (Rule 307) — existing French comments are not rewritten wholesale, but any new or edited comment is in English
- Commit messages: **English only** (Rule 307)
- UI text and logs: **English US only** (Rule 129)
- Bubbletea models define their own message types
- Use `theme` package for consistent styling (`internal/ui/theme/`)
- Config changes must call `config.Save()` to persist
- All colors defined in `theme/colors.go`, all styles in `theme/styles.go`
- Message naming: `[ComponentName][Action]Msg` (e.g., `ComponentFormSubmitMsg`)
- Context names: the rule exists twice (`config.ValidateContextName`, `contextcmd.ValidName`); change both or neither (`TestContextNameRulesAgree`). Creation refuses `-`, `new`, `list` (`config.ValidateNewContextName`); loading does not (D91)

## Critical Bubble Tea Rules

**NEVER modify model state inside a Cmd** (Rule 110) - Race condition:
- `Update()` is the ONLY place to modify model state
- `View()` is read-only
- `Cmd` functions do I/O and return messages

**NEVER use `style.Render()` inside `table.Row{}`** (Rule 122) - ANSI sequences corrupt all subsequent rows:
- Use plain text: `theme.IconError + " error"` not `theme.StatusErrorStyle.Render(...)`
- Apply row styling via `table.SetStyles(theme.TableStylesForState("error"))`

**Update() case extraction**: If a case block exceeds 5 lines, extract to `handle[MessageType]()` method returning `(tea.Model, tea.Cmd)`

# Planning Rules

## Implementation Plans

- **Location**: Always write implementation plans to `.claude/plans/` in the current project directory.
- **Format**: Use Markdown format for plans.
- **Naming**: Use descriptive names like `feature-name-plan.md` or `YYYY-MM-DD-feature-name.md`.

## Antigravity IDE Integration

When using the Antigravity IDE extension:
- Save all implementation plans to `.claude/plans/` relative to the project root.
- Create the directory if it doesn't exist before saving plans.
- Plans should be accessible from both Claude Code CLI and Antigravity IDE.

# TUI — Rule index

TUI rules are split across 5 topic files:

| File | Rules | Content |
|---------|--------|---------|
| [`tui-layout.md`](tui-layout.md) | 101, 107, 108, 111, 112, 123, 124, 130, 134, 137, 138 | General layout, keybindings, viewport, tabs, shortcuts header, format descriptions, shortcuts obviousness |
| [`tui-theme.md`](tui-theme.md) | 102, 105, 115, 117, 118, 119, 127, 129 | Colors, lipgloss background, `theme.*` helpers, language |
| [`tui-forms.md`](tui-forms.md) | 103, 104, 113, 114, 120, 121, 131, 132, 133, 135 | Forms, modals, focus, status icons, value cycling, WrappedInput, key assignment |
| [`tui-tables.md`](tui-tables.md) | 106, 116, 122, 125, 136, 139 | Tables, column widths, plain-text cells + color via `Style`, filter bar, body never replaced (spinner or message) |
| [`tui-behavior.md`](tui-behavior.md) | 109, 110, 126, 128 | Bubble Tea (Cmd/Update), scan cache, footer messages (three levels, one component) |

## Critical rules (summary)

**Rule 110** — NEVER modify the model inside a `Cmd` → race condition. Only `Update()` modifies the model.

**Rule 122** — `Cell` returns plain text (it gets measured), color goes through `Style`. A `style.Render(...)` inside `Cell` gets truncated in the middle of its escape sequence and bleeds onto every following row.

**Rule 128** — A footer message goes through `components.FooterMessage`: three levels (neutral info, orange warning, red error), always centered, a single implementation. A table's loading state is shown in the footer with a spinner, never in the body.

**Rule 139** — A `datatable`'s body is always `m.table.View()`, never a spinner or a message: an empty table (loading, nothing to list, a filter with no results) stays a table — a header, no rows. The count goes in `GetHeaderInfo`, the status in the footer.

**Rule 129** — All UI text and all logs in **English US**.

**Rule 133** — `bubbles/textarea` is forbidden. Use `components.WrappedInput` for any multi-line text field.

The per-topic TUI rule files above load when a matching file is read or edited; when reviewing a diff without opening files, read them explicitly.

# entire-graph — instructions for coding agents (follow directly)

You have a deterministic local code graph: `entire graph` (functions, classes, methods,
types, routes + call/inheritance relations; no network). These instructions are FOR YOU, the
agent reading this file. Use the graph to narrow exploration without trading away correctness.

## The workflow (mandatory for locate/fix/change tasks)

Your FIRST action on any task that requires finding code must be ONE search:

    entire graph search --repo . --profile full --query "<the task or bug in one sentence>"

Then open the top hit's file with your file-read tool (pass a line range around the reported
line), inspect enough surrounding behavior to justify the change, and make the smallest complete
edit. Treat graph output as evidence, not an oracle.

## Hard rules

1. SEARCH FIRST — never grep/find/cat to locate code before you have searched.
2. READ focused source around the result. Widen the check when aliases, generated code, dynamic
   dispatch, or related implementations could matter.
3. Use graph follow-ups only when they answer a real question. For impact or callers, prefer:
       entire graph impact --repo . --symbol X
4. Make the smallest complete edit and check sibling sites or contracts when the task implies them.
5. VERIFY before stopping. Run the most focused relevant test, build, or reproduction available.
   If execution is unavailable, perform a bounded source-level verification and state the limit.
6. Prefer precise queries and line ranges, but never trade resolution for fewer turns.
7. Feature-detect before relying on semantic relations:
       entire graph capabilities --json

## When NOT to use the graph

If the task already names the exact file and it is small, just read it — the graph saves tokens
by eliminating exploration; when there is nothing to explore, skip it.

## Reference

    locate  ->  entire graph search --repo . --profile full --query "..."
    impact  ->  entire graph impact --repo . --symbol X   (one shot: callers, callees, type consumers, data flow, co-change, siblings)
    callers ->  entire graph neighbors --repo . --symbol X --relation CALLS --direction in
    change  ->  entire graph diff --base A --head B --json
    detect  ->  entire graph capabilities --json   (inventory-only languages have no relations)
    stats   ->  entire graph stats --repo .        (human-facing token-savings report; not part of your workflow — do not run it unless asked)

# CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **AI Collaboration Rule**:
> - **Planning**, **Brainstorming**, **Implementation** and **Bug fixes** are all
>   in scope. Planning is no longer delegated to Gemini (Antigravity).
> - Implementation plans go in `.claude/plans/` (see
>   [rules/planning.md](rules/planning.md)); design decisions that outlive a plan
>   are recorded in `docs/backlog.md`. Open work (stories, tasks, bugs) is tracked
>   in Plane, see the `## Plane` section of the root `CLAUDE.md`.
> - Always refer to [project-context.md](../project-context.md) for global project rules.
>   It sits in this repository, at the root. The absolute path this line used to
>   carry named a GitLab checkout that is no longer where DevDesk lives.

## Project Overview

DevDesk is a terminal-based TUI (Text User Interface) application built with Go and Bubble Tea framework. It provides DevSecOps functionality including:
- System status monitoring (HTTP/HTTPS, ICMP, DNS, SSL checks)
- GitLab integration (authentication, project explorer, multi-select clone)
- Security scanning (Trivy CVE/secret/license/misconfig + Gitleaks secrets)
- Container management with real-time metrics, on Docker or Podman (`app.container_engine`)
- OCI resource management (image scanning, container launching, network inspection)
- Network diagnostics (DNS, route, ICMP, TCP, TLS, HTTP) + real-time port monitoring + this machine's interfaces + local port forwarding (unprivileged, loopback only)
- Multi-context configuration management via YAML
- Local workspaces management with git metadata
- Claude Code session list (`:agent-usage` / `:au`): sessions found on this machine, by project and date, and per session the agent tree (orchestrator and sub-agents: types, models, tokens, share of the total; sortable by Total; also per agent a state (running / idle / done / unknown, idle after 5 min without a transcript line) shown as a status dot in the first column (the `running` dot blinks, DEVDESK-151) and as text, tool calls and duration; and an indicative cost per agent, `Est. cost` (orange from 75 % and red from 90 % of the session's estimated cost, when at least two agents are priced), from prices you write in the context YAML (`agent_usage.prices`, none shipped), with the session's `Billed` cost and `Unattributed` in the header, DEVDESK-47; a `Breakdown` colour bar per agent and, with `tab` inside a session, a Breakdown tab splitting the whole session's tokens by category, model and agent, as a percentage of tokens, DEVDESK-98). An open session updates live: read again every 2 s while active, only what was appended; paused after 5 min with no write and no unfinished sub-agent, or when its transcript is gone (header `Updates › paused`); `ctrl+r` reads it again in full. The sessions list itself is not live.

## Build and Development Commands

Tasks live in `mise.toml` — there is no Makefile. `mise tasks` lists them all.

```bash
# Development (fastest)
mise run dev          # Run directly with go run
go run .

# Build
mise run build        # Build binary to bin/dk
mise run run          # Build and run

# Testing
mise run test         # Run all tests
mise run cover        # Coverage per package
go test -v ./...      # Run all tests with verbose output
go test ./internal/command  # Run tests for specific package
mise run test-race    # Detect race conditions (critical for Bubble Tea Cmds)

# Code Quality
mise run fmt          # Format code
mise run vet          # Run go vet
mise run lint         # MANDATORY before commits - golangci-lint
mise run tidy         # Tidy dependencies
mise run check        # fmt + vet + lint + test in one go

# Installation
mise run install      # Install to $GOPATH/bin
```

`test-race` needs cgo and therefore a C compiler (`gcc`/`clang`) on `PATH`.

## Git, worktrees, pull requests — absolute rules

- Work happens in a worktree under `.worktrees/<branch>`, created from `origin/main`; the main checkout stays clean, on `main`.
- Never push directly to `main`: the Entire mirror rejects it, and so does the `main-protection` ruleset. Everything goes through a PR, merged once `Lint and build` and `Test` are green.
- Always use `gh -R anthnel/devdesk` (`origin` is `entire://`). There is one remote, `origin`; do not add a second one pointing at GitHub.
- A red `Entire Gates` check caused by Approvals alone does not block a merge (Findings, Checks, Up to date must stay green).
- In a sandbox, only commit; the host pushes, opens the PR and merges. Whoever creates a worktree removes it (never `git worktree prune` from the other side). The sandbox creates its own worktree; the host never creates one for it.
- Before creating a worktree or branch, pushing, opening/merging a PR or removing a worktree, load the `git-worktree-pr` skill.

## Releases

Only merging the release-please PR publishes a release; never merge it without the user's explicit agreement. After every merge on main, the orchestrating session loads the `release-flow` skill and checks the triggers.

### Status Monitoring System

**Factory Pattern for Checkers:**
- `internal/status/checker.go` - Main orchestrator
- `internal/status/http_checker.go` - HTTP/HTTPS checks
- `internal/status/icmp_checker.go` - ICMP ping checks
- `internal/status/dns_checker.go` - DNS resolution checks

Each checker implements `CheckerInterface`. The main `Checker.CheckOne()` uses a factory pattern to instantiate the right checker based on `component.Type`.

**Parallel Execution:**
- `CheckAll()` runs all component checks concurrently using goroutines and sync.WaitGroup
- Results are collected and returned as `[]ComponentStatus`

### Component CRUD Operations

Status view supports adding/editing/deleting monitors:
- `internal/ui/status/components/component_form.go` - Form component
- `internal/ui/status/components/confirm_modal.go` - Confirmation dialog
- Changes persist to `~/.devdesk/config.yaml` via `config.Save()`

State flags in Model: `creating`, `editing`, `confirming`, `selectedIdx`

### Credentials Management

No secret DevDesk holds is written to a file DevDesk owns. `internal/credentials`
implements the `Storage` interface three ways and `Select()` picks exactly one —
writing to several at once is what let the old "secure" option store a token in
the credential manager *and* in plaintext:

| Storage | Backend | Notes |
|---------|---------|-------|
| `KeyringStorage` | Windows Credential Manager / macOS Keychain / Secret Service | via `zalando/go-keyring`, no cgo. The default. |
| `GitCredentialStorage` | git's configured credential helper | Only when the helper is not `store`, which writes plaintext. Context-aware. |
| `MemoryStorage` | this process | Last resort, and deliberately worse: the auth view says nothing was saved. |

`Select(context, preference)` returns a `Selection{Storage, Backend, Detail}`.
The order is keyring → git credential → memory; `app.secret_backend` in the
context config pins the head of it (`auto`, `keyring`, `git-credential`). A
pinned backend that is unreachable falls through to memory rather than silently
to the other one.

The router resolves one `Selection` per context and keeps it in
`shared.State.Secrets`. It must be reused for the lifetime of the context — a
second `Select()` call yields a fresh `MemoryStorage` that cannot see what the
first one holds.

`MigrateLegacySecrets` runs at startup and on every context switch: a
`gitlab.token` or `registry.password` left in a context file by an older build
is moved into the store and deleted from the YAML, with the result reported in
the auth view.

## Testing

Test files follow Go conventions (`*_test.go`):
- `internal/command/parser_test.go` - Command parser tests
- `internal/app/app_test.go` - App router tests

Use table-driven tests where appropriate.

**`go test` does not detect races or explore fuzz targets.** `mise run test` runs
only the fuzz seeds, so `internal/agentusage` concurrency tests
(`TestConcurrent*`) need `mise run test-race`. To explore `FuzzIncrementalMatchesFull`
run `go test -fuzz=FuzzIncrementalMatchesFull -fuzztime=60s ./internal/agentusage`.

**HOME is shared across a test process.** `TestMain` in `internal/app` sets
`HOME` once for the whole process, so under `go test -count=N` a test finds
the files its own previous run wrote (context config, forge index cache), and
it fails from `-count=2` while `-count=1` passes (DEVDESK-36). A test that
writes under HOME isolates it with `t.Setenv("HOME", t.TempDir())` and
`USERPROFILE` too; in `internal/app`, call `isolateHome(t)` from
`harness_test.go` (already done by `routerAt`). `internal/ui/setup` is fixed
(DEVDESK-38): its `isolateHome(t)` helper in `model_test.go` is called by the
tests that write under HOME. Other packages whose TestMain does
`os.Setenv("HOME", …)` may have the same default. To find them:
`grep -rn 'os.Setenv("HOME"' --include=*_test.go`, then `go test -count=2` on each package.

**Never get a "free" port by `net.Listen("tcp", "127.0.0.1:0")`, reading the
port, then `Close()`, and letting the code under test bind it later.** Between
the close and the bind, any `bind(0)` can be handed that very port: an
`httptest.NewServer` in the same test, another test, another process on the
runner. The symptom is an intermittent `address already in use`, mostly in CI
(Linux gave the just-closed port back to about 1 `bind(0)` in 7,000; DEVDESK-35,
D85 in `docs/backlog.md`).

- If the code under test takes a port, call `loopback.ReservePort(t)`
  (`internal/testutil/loopback`). On Linux it holds a socket bound with
  `SO_REUSEADDR`, never listening, until `t.Cleanup`: `bind(0)` and `connect()`
  cannot take the port, but `net.Listen` can.
- Otherwise let the server bind `:0` and read the real port, or keep the
  listener open and hand it to the code under test.
- Off Linux, `ReservePort` keeps the old behavior and the window stays open
  (on Windows Go does not set `SO_REUSEADDR`). That is known, not a local bug.
- `internal/testutil/loopback` is imported from `_test.go` files only; nothing
  enforces it yet.

**Test input and colour (DEVDESK-199).** Build keys only through
`internal/ui/testutil` (`Key`, `Keys`, `Type`, `Paste`, `Text`, `IsText`), never a
literal `tea.KeyMsg` or `tea.Key*`. `Key` is strict: an unknown name panics. The
space key is built as a key (`KeySpace` + rune `' '`), never matched through
`String()` (v1 `" "`, v2 `"space"`). The colour profile is forced through
`internal/testutil/colorprofile` (`TrueColor(t)`, `Force()` in `TestMain`), the only
importer of termenv; it is a leaf package because testutil→shortcut→theme would
cycle. `internal/ui/testutil/source_guard_test.go` fails the suite on a hand-built
key, a termenv import or `SetColorProfile` in any `_test.go`. Paste tests
(`internal/app/paste_test.go`, `wrapped_input_test.go`, `component_form_test.go`):
a paste reaches the focused field, newlines become spaces in single-line fields,
and no key action fires (Rule 111).

**Space and key API (DEVDESK-200).** Production code matches the space key as
`keymap.Space`, never `" "`/`"space"`, and reads keys through `String()` only
(no `.Runes`, `.Alt`, `.Paste`, `tea.KeyType` or `tea.Key<Name>`). Two guards in
`internal/ui/keymap` (`space_scan_test.go`, `legacy_key_scan_test.go`) fail the
suite otherwise; limits are listed in `docs/architecture/app-shell.md`.

## Dependencies

Key libraries (see `go.mod`):
- `github.com/charmbracelet/bubbletea` - TUI framework
- `github.com/charmbracelet/bubbles` - Pre-built TUI components (table, textinput, spinner)
- `github.com/charmbracelet/lipgloss` - Styling
- `gitlab.com/gitlab-org/api/client-go` - GitLab API client
- `github.com/prometheus-community/pro-bing` - ICMP ping functionality (maintained fork of go-ping/ping)
- `github.com/google/go-github/v68` - GitHub API client (§3.6)
- `github.com/libp2p/go-netroute` - which interface a destination leaves by, on all three platforms (§3.44)
- `github.com/zalando/go-keyring` - host secret manager (wincred / Keychain / Secret Service), no cgo
- `gopkg.in/yaml.v3` - YAML configuration

## Code Conventions

- Comments: **English only** (Rule 307) — existing French comments are not rewritten wholesale, but any new or edited comment is in English
- Commit messages: **English only** (Rule 307)
- UI text and logs: **English US only** (Rule 129)
- Bubbletea models define their own message types
- Use `theme` package for consistent styling (`internal/ui/theme/`)
- Config changes must call `config.Save()` to persist
- All colors defined in `theme/colors.go`, all styles in `theme/styles.go`
- Message naming: `[ComponentName][Action]Msg` (e.g., `ComponentFormSubmitMsg`)
- Context names: the rule exists twice (`config.ValidateContextName`, `contextcmd.ValidName`); change both or neither (`TestContextNameRulesAgree`). Creation refuses `-`, `new`, `list` (`config.ValidateNewContextName`); loading does not (D91)

## Critical Bubble Tea Rules

**NEVER modify model state inside a Cmd** (Rule 110) - Race condition:
- `Update()` is the ONLY place to modify model state
- `View()` is read-only
- `Cmd` functions do I/O and return messages

**NEVER use `style.Render()` inside `table.Row{}`** (Rule 122) - ANSI sequences corrupt all subsequent rows:
- Use plain text: `theme.IconError + " error"` not `theme.StatusErrorStyle.Render(...)`
- Apply row styling via `table.SetStyles(theme.TableStylesForState("error"))`

**Update() case extraction**: If a case block exceeds 5 lines, extract to `handle[MessageType]()` method returning `(tea.Model, tea.Cmd)`

# TUI — Rule index

TUI rules are split across 5 topic files:

| File | Rules | Content |
|---------|--------|---------|
| [`tui-layout.md`](tui-layout.md) | 101, 107, 108, 111, 112, 123, 124, 130, 134, 137, 138 | General layout, keybindings, viewport, tabs, shortcuts header, format descriptions, shortcuts obviousness |
| [`tui-theme.md`](tui-theme.md) | 102, 105, 115, 117, 118, 119, 127, 129 | Colors, lipgloss background, `theme.*` helpers, language |
| [`tui-forms.md`](tui-forms.md) | 103, 104, 113, 114, 120, 121, 131, 132, 133, 135 | Forms, modals, focus, status icons, value cycling, WrappedInput, key assignment |
| [`tui-tables.md`](tui-tables.md) | 106, 116, 122, 125, 136, 139 | Tables, column widths, plain-text cells + color via `Style`, filter bar, body never replaced (spinner or message) |
| [`tui-behavior.md`](tui-behavior.md) | 109, 110, 126, 128 | Bubble Tea (Cmd/Update), scan cache, footer messages (three levels, one component) |

## Critical rules (summary)

**Rule 110** — NEVER modify the model inside a `Cmd` → race condition. Only `Update()` modifies the model.

**Rule 122** — `Cell` returns plain text (it gets measured), color goes through `Style`. A `style.Render(...)` inside `Cell` gets truncated in the middle of its escape sequence and bleeds onto every following row.

**Rule 128** — A footer message goes through `components.FooterMessage`: three levels (neutral info, orange warning, red error), always centered, a single implementation. A table's loading state is shown in the footer with a spinner, never in the body.

**Rule 139** — A `datatable`'s body is always `m.table.View()`, never a spinner or a message: an empty table (loading, nothing to list, a filter with no results) stays a table — a header, no rows. The count goes in `GetHeaderInfo`, the status in the footer.

**Rule 129** — All UI text and all logs in **English US**.

**Rule 133** — `bubbles/textarea` is forbidden. Use `components.WrappedInput` for any multi-line text field.

The per-topic TUI rule files above load when a matching file is read or edited; when reviewing a diff without opening files, read them explicitly.

# entire-graph — instructions for coding agents (follow directly)

You have a deterministic local code graph: `entire graph` (functions, classes, methods,
types, routes + call/inheritance relations; no network). These instructions are FOR YOU, the
agent reading this file. Use the graph to narrow exploration without trading away correctness.

## The workflow (mandatory for locate/fix/change tasks)

Your FIRST action on any task that requires finding code must be ONE search:

    entire graph search --repo . --profile full --query "<the task or bug in one sentence>"

Then open the top hit's file with your file-read tool (pass a line range around the reported
line), inspect enough surrounding behavior to justify the change, and make the smallest complete
edit. Treat graph output as evidence, not an oracle.

## Hard rules

1. SEARCH FIRST — never grep/find/cat to locate code before you have searched.
2. READ focused source around the result. Widen the check when aliases, generated code, dynamic
   dispatch, or related implementations could matter.
3. Use graph follow-ups only when they answer a real question. For impact or callers, prefer:
       entire graph impact --repo . --symbol X
4. Make the smallest complete edit and check sibling sites or contracts when the task implies them.
5. VERIFY before stopping. Run the most focused relevant test, build, or reproduction available.
   If execution is unavailable, perform a bounded source-level verification and state the limit.
6. Prefer precise queries and line ranges, but never trade resolution for fewer turns.
7. Feature-detect before relying on semantic relations:
       entire graph capabilities --json

## When NOT to use the graph

If the task already names the exact file and it is small, just read it — the graph saves tokens
by eliminating exploration; when there is nothing to explore, skip it.

    locate  ->  entire graph search --repo . --profile full --query "..."

# CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **AI Collaboration Rule**:
> - **Planning**, **Brainstorming**, **Implementation** and **Bug fixes** are all
>   in scope. Planning is no longer delegated to Gemini (Antigravity).
> - Implementation plans go in `.claude/plans/` (see
>   [rules/planning.md](rules/planning.md)); design decisions that outlive a plan
>   are recorded in `docs/backlog.md`. Open work (stories, tasks, bugs) is tracked
>   in Plane, see the `## Plane` section of the root `CLAUDE.md`.
> - Always refer to [project-context.md](../project-context.md) for global project rules.
>   It sits in this repository, at the root. The absolute path this line used to
>   carry named a GitLab checkout that is no longer where DevDesk lives.

## Project Overview

DevDesk is a terminal-based TUI (Text User Interface) application built with Go and Bubble Tea framework. It provides DevSecOps functionality including:
- System status monitoring (HTTP/HTTPS, ICMP, DNS, SSL checks)
- GitLab integration (authentication, project explorer, multi-select clone)
- Security scanning (Trivy CVE/secret/license/misconfig + Gitleaks secrets)
- Container management with real-time metrics, on Docker or Podman (`app.container_engine`)
- OCI resource management (image scanning, container launching, network inspection)
- Network diagnostics (DNS, route, ICMP, TCP, TLS, HTTP) + real-time port monitoring + this machine's interfaces + local port forwarding (unprivileged, loopback only)
- Multi-context configuration management via YAML
- Local workspaces management with git metadata
- Claude Code session list (`:agent-usage` / `:au`): sessions found on this machine, by project and date, and per session the agent tree (orchestrator and sub-agents: types, models, tokens, share of the total; sortable by Total; also per agent a state (running / idle / done / unknown, idle after 5 min without a transcript line) shown as a status dot in the first column (the `running` dot blinks, DEVDESK-151) and as text, tool calls and duration; and an indicative cost per agent, `Est. cost` (orange from 75 % and red from 90 % of the session's estimated cost, when at least two agents are priced), from prices you write in the context YAML (`agent_usage.prices`, none shipped), with the session's `Billed` cost and `Unattributed` in the header, DEVDESK-47; a `Breakdown` colour bar per agent and, with `tab` inside a session, a Breakdown tab splitting the whole session's tokens by category, model and agent, as a percentage of tokens, DEVDESK-98). An open session updates live: read again every 2 s while active, only what was appended; paused after 5 min with no write and no unfinished sub-agent, or when its transcript is gone (header `Updates › paused`); `ctrl+r` reads it again in full. The sessions list itself is not live.

## Build and Development Commands

Tasks live in `mise.toml` — there is no Makefile. `mise tasks` lists them all.

```bash
# Development (fastest)
mise run dev          # Run directly with go run
go run .

# Build
mise run build        # Build binary to bin/dk
mise run run          # Build and run

# Testing
mise run test         # Run all tests
mise run cover        # Coverage per package
go test -v ./...      # Run all tests with verbose output
go test ./internal/command  # Run tests for specific package
mise run test-race    # Detect race conditions (critical for Bubble Tea Cmds)

# Code Quality
mise run fmt          # Format code
mise run vet          # Run go vet
mise run lint         # MANDATORY before commits - golangci-lint
mise run tidy         # Tidy dependencies
mise run check        # fmt + vet + lint + test in one go

# Installation
mise run install      # Install to $GOPATH/bin
```

`test-race` needs cgo and therefore a C compiler (`gcc`/`clang`) on `PATH`.

## Git, worktrees, pull requests — absolute rules

- Work happens in a worktree under `.worktrees/<branch>`, created from `origin/main`; the main checkout stays clean, on `main`.
- Never push directly to `main`: the Entire mirror rejects it, and so does the `main-protection` ruleset. Everything goes through a PR, merged once `Lint and build` and `Test` are green.
- Always use `gh -R anthnel/devdesk` (`origin` is `entire://`). There is one remote, `origin`; do not add a second one pointing at GitHub.
- A red `Entire Gates` check caused by Approvals alone does not block a merge (Findings, Checks, Up to date must stay green).
- In a sandbox, only commit; the host pushes, opens the PR and merges. Whoever creates a worktree removes it (never `git worktree prune` from the other side). The sandbox creates its own worktree; the host never creates one for it.
- Before creating a worktree or branch, pushing, opening/merging a PR or removing a worktree, load the `git-worktree-pr` skill.

## Releases

Only merging the release-please PR publishes a release; never merge it without the user's explicit agreement. After every merge on main, the orchestrating session loads the `release-flow` skill and checks the triggers.

### Status Monitoring System

**Factory Pattern for Checkers:**
- `internal/status/checker.go` - Main orchestrator
- `internal/status/http_checker.go` - HTTP/HTTPS checks
- `internal/status/icmp_checker.go` - ICMP ping checks
- `internal/status/dns_checker.go` - DNS resolution checks

Each checker implements `CheckerInterface`. The main `Checker.CheckOne()` uses a factory pattern to instantiate the right checker based on `component.Type`.

**Parallel Execution:**
- `CheckAll()` runs all component checks concurrently using goroutines and sync.WaitGroup
- Results are collected and returned as `[]ComponentStatus`

### Component CRUD Operations

Status view supports adding/editing/deleting monitors:
- `internal/ui/status/components/component_form.go` - Form component
- `internal/ui/status/components/confirm_modal.go` - Confirmation dialog
- Changes persist to `~/.devdesk/config.yaml` via `config.Save()`

State flags in Model: `creating`, `editing`, `confirming`, `selectedIdx`

### Credentials Management

No secret DevDesk holds is written to a file DevDesk owns. `internal/credentials`
implements the `Storage` interface three ways and `Select()` picks exactly one —
writing to several at once is what let the old "secure" option store a token in
the credential manager *and* in plaintext:

| Storage | Backend | Notes |
|---------|---------|-------|
| `KeyringStorage` | Windows Credential Manager / macOS Keychain / Secret Service | via `zalando/go-keyring`, no cgo. The default. |
| `GitCredentialStorage` | git's configured credential helper | Only when the helper is not `store`, which writes plaintext. Context-aware. |
| `MemoryStorage` | this process | Last resort, and deliberately worse: the auth view says nothing was saved. |

`Select(context, preference)` returns a `Selection{Storage, Backend, Detail}`.
The order is keyring → git credential → memory; `app.secret_backend` in the

pinned backend that is unreachable falls through to memory rather than silently
to the other one.

`shared.State.Secrets`. It must be reused for the lifetime of the context — a
second `Select()` call yields a fresh `MemoryStorage` that cannot see what the
first one holds.

`gitlab.token` or `registry.password` left in a context file by an older build

`HOME` once for the whole process, so under `go test -count=N` a test finds
the files its own previous run wrote (context config, forge index cache), and
it fails from `-count=2` while `-count=1` passes (DEVDESK-36). A test that
writes under HOME isolates it with `t.Setenv("HOME", t.TempDir())` and
`USERPROFILE` too; in `internal/app`, call `isolateHome(t)` from
`harness_test.go` (already done by `routerAt`). `internal/ui/setup` is fixed
(DEVDESK-38): its `isolateHome(t)` helper in `model_test.go` is called by the
tests that write under HOME. Other packages whose TestMain does

`grep -rn 'os.Setenv("HOME"' --include=*_test.go`, then `go test -count=2` on each package.

**Never get a "free" port by `net.Listen("tcp", "127.0.0.1:0")`, reading the
port, then `Close()`, and letting the code under test bind it later.** Between
the close and the bind, any `bind(0)` can be handed that very port: an
`httptest.NewServer` in the same test, another test, another process on the
runner. The symptom is an intermittent `address already in use`, mostly in CI
(Linux gave the just-closed port back to about 1 `bind(0)` in 7,000; DEVDESK-35,
D85 in `docs/backlog.md`).

- If the code under test takes a port, call `loopback.ReservePort(t)`
  (`internal/testutil/loopback`). On Linux it holds a socket bound with
  `SO_REUSEADDR`, never listening, until `t.Cleanup`: `bind(0)` and `connect()`
  cannot take the port, but `net.Listen` can.
- Otherwise let the server bind `:0` and read the real port, or keep the
  listener open and hand it to the code under test.
- Off Linux, `ReservePort` keeps the old behavior and the window stays open
  (on Windows Go does not set `SO_REUSEADDR`). That is known, not a local bug.

**Rule 122** — `Cell` returns plain text (it gets measured), color goes through `Style`. A `style.Render(...)` inside `Cell` gets truncated in the middle of its escape sequence and bleeds onto every following row.

**Rule 128** — A footer message goes through `components.FooterMessage`: three levels (neutral info, orange warning, red error), always centered, a single implementation. A table's loading state is shown in the footer with a spinner, never in the body.

**Rule 139** — A `datatable`'s body is always `m.table.View()`, never a spinner or a message: an empty table (loading, nothing to list, a filter with no results) stays a table — a header, no rows. The count goes in `GetHeaderInfo`, the status in the footer.

**Rule 129** — All UI text and all logs in **English US**.

**Rule 133** — `bubbles/textarea` is forbidden. Use `components.WrappedInput` for any multi-line text field.

99	## Strategy: TDD when the intermediate commits do not compile
100	
101	The `charm.land/*/v2` stack is coupled: `internal/app` imports every view, every view imports
102	`components`, which imports `textinput` and `theme`. **No commit between A1 and E builds the whole
103	module.** The commits are review units, not bisect points (spike §9). So:
104	
105	1. **One branch, linear order A → G**, one commit per step (A and D split into sub-commits). Each
106	   commit changes one *category* across all files. Fixes found later for an earlier category go in
107	   the current commit and are noted in its body ("also: …"). Rewriting history to move them back
108	   is possible without an editor (`GIT_SEQUENCE_EDITOR=: git rebase -i --autosquash origin/main`
109	   with `fixup!` commits) but not required.
110	2. **Tests are written first in each step**, by the tester, from the "Tests" list of the step. A
111	   test is red for one of three reasons, stated per test:
112	   - **[R-assert]** it compiles and fails on today's code (e.g. theme validation, runewidth of a
113	     flag, the `KeyPressMsg` guard). Prove it red before the change.
114	   - **[R-compile]** it is written against the v2 API and does not compile until the step ends.
115	     The red proof is the compile error itself (`go vet ./<pkg>` output pasted in the progress file).
116	   - **[C]** characterization: green before and after (a guard that must not break). Prove it can

all categories in each file, and the PR has to be split by category. See H1.

## Blocking questions (user)

None blocks the start (steps A to F). Q1 and Q2 block the **close** of the story (done criterion);
the orchestrator asks them before the PR is opened.

1. **Pass threshold for `TestMeasureRedrawCost`.** The criterion says "compared to the reference"
   but sets no threshold. Options: (a) report only: the numbers go to the backlog and never block
   the merge; (b) the merge blocks if `bytes/s` of `blink-20` or `spinner-20` rises by more than
   25 % over v1 on the same machine, or if `redraws/s` exceeds the tick cadence (2 and 10); otherwise
   a follow-up story; (c) a strict "no worse than v1". **Recommendation: (b).** The v2 renderer
   also writes terminal queries (DECRQM 2026/2027) and synchronized-output brackets that v1 did
   not, so (c) could fail on bytes that cost nothing on screen.
2. **Manual check matrix** (impact report §5 Q6, still open). Who runs it, and on which terminals:
   `dk.exe` in Windows Terminal, WSL in Windows Terminal, macOS Terminal.app or iTerm2, tmux?
   **Recommendation: the user, at least Windows Terminal (`dk.exe`) and WSL**, on the checklist of
   step G2. No TTY is available to the agents; the spike ran nothing in a real terminal.

## Hypotheses (prudent default, no question)

- **H1. The spike is a reference, not a seed.** Each step is redone by category with scripts (kept in
  the scratchpad, quoted in the commit body), checking against `git diff 63ebd72 217b389`. Before
  starting, pin the object so `git gc` cannot drop it: `git update-ref refs/spike/charm-v2 217b389`
  (local, never pushed).
- **H2. The colour-profile helper goes no-op in A2, not in F.** `lipgloss.SetColorProfile` does not
  exist in v2, and the tests of `theme`, `overlay`, `shortcut`, `datatable`, `components` import
  `internal/testutil/colorprofile`: without that change none of them compiles before F, and A
  has no green checkpoint. F keeps everything else about the profile: `termenv` out of `go.mod`, the
  helper's own test deleted, the source guard re-aimed, `main.go`, `ansi.Strip` in the 7 tests.
- **H3. Invalid theme hex (user decision 1).** `LoadTheme` validates and returns an error naming the
  key and the value. The whole theme is refused. A **non-empty** value that is not `#rgb` / `#rrggbb`
  is invalid; an **empty** value keeps today's behaviour (fallback for optional keys). The callers'
  behaviour is unchanged: `main.go` logs and keeps the default theme, `App.applyThemeNow` logs and
  keeps the current one (no footer message added; a follow-up if the user wants one).
- **H4. `WT_SESSION` (user decision 2).** `main.go` passes `tea.WithColorProfile(colorprofile.TrueColor)`
  when `WT_SESSION` is set **and `NO_COLOR` is not**. A forced profile bypasses the detection that
  honours `NO_COLOR` (`colorprofile.Detect`). The `COLORTERM` workaround is deleted.
- **H5. All 115 production `tea.KeyMsg` become `tea.KeyPressMsg`.** Step (b) of the criteria says
  "(KeyPressMsg)". A guard then refuses the interface in production. Tests keep `tea.KeyMsg` where
  they only hold a value (it is an interface that `KeyPressMsg` satisfies).
- **H6. `setView` panics on a non-`Screen`.** `a.setView(name, m tea.Model)` is the only place that
  asserts `.(Screen)`. A view that stops implementing `Render` is a programming error; Bubble Tea
  recovers the panic and restores the terminal. The panic message names the view.
- **H7. Squash-merge as usual.** The seven commits are review units inside the PR (say so in its
  body). `gh pr merge --squash` keeps them visible in the PR, not on `main`. PR title:
  `refactor: move to Charm v2 (Bubble Tea, Bubbles, Lip Gloss, ntcharts) (DEVDESK-201)`.
- **H8. No ADR.** The project records lasting decisions in `docs/backlog.md` (D entries). Step G
  writes them (option C, `KeyPressMsg` only, paste routing, redraw comparison).

## Strategy: TDD when the intermediate commits do not compile

The `charm.land/*/v2` stack is coupled: `internal/app` imports every view, every view imports
`components`, which imports `textinput` and `theme`. **No commit between A1 and E builds the whole
module.** The commits are review units, not bisect points (spike §9). So:

1. **One branch, linear order A → G**, one commit per step (A and D split into sub-commits). Each
   commit changes one *category* across all files. Fixes found later for an earlier category go in
   the current commit and are noted in its body ("also: …"). Rewriting history to move them back
   is possible without an editor (`GIT_SEQUENCE_EDITOR=: git rebase -i --autosquash origin/main`
   with `fixup!` commits) but not required.
2. **Tests are written first in each step**, by the tester, from the "Tests" list of the step. A
   test is red for one of three reasons, stated per test:
   - **[R-assert]** it compiles and fails on today's code (e.g. theme validation, runewidth of a
     flag, the `KeyPressMsg` guard). Prove it red before the change.
   - **[R-compile]** it is written against the v2 API and does not compile until the step ends.
     The red proof is the compile error itself (`go vet ./<pkg>` output pasted in the progress file).
   - **[C]** characterization: green before and after (a guard that must not break). Prove it can
     fail by injecting the fault once (the detector self-tests already do this for the AST guards).
3. **Compile frontier.** Each step ends with a check that the frontier moved:
   - the packages listed under "Green checkpoint" build and their tests pass;
   - `go vet ./... 2>&1 | grep -cE '<pattern of the category just handled>'` is 0 (patterns per
     step below). The full error list goes to the scratchpad, never to the repo.
4. First `go build ./...` green: end of **E**. First `go test ./...` green: end of **F**.
   `mise run check` and `mise run test-race` green: end of **F**, again at the end of **G**.

## Branch and worktree

Load the `git-worktree-pr` skill first. From the main checkout:

```
git fetch origin
git worktree add .worktrees/feat/DEVDESK-201-charm-v2 -b feat/DEVDESK-201-charm-v2 origin/main
git update-ref refs/spike/charm-v2 217b389
```

All work happens in `.worktrees/feat/DEVDESK-201-charm-v2`. Push and PR only at the end of G, after
`mise run check` and `mise run test-race`. Review with `dev-team:large-diff-review`.

## Order of work

```
A1 imports + go.mod ─► A2 theme ─► B keys ─► C router (option C) ─► D1 bubbles API ─► D2 viewport guard ─► D3 paste in forms ─► E ntcharts + widths ─► F colour profile ─► G1 docs ─► G2 measures + manual checks
```

Strictly sequential (one worktree, coupled build). Parallel work possible:
- the tester writes the tests of step N+1 while the coder finishes step N (different files);
- G1 (rules and architecture docs) can be drafted from the end of C, since the design no longer moves;
- the v1 half of the redraw measurement (G2) can run at any time on `origin/main` in another worktree.

---

**Files.** `go.mod`, `go.sum`, and every `.go` file importing a Charm v1 path: about 376 files
(bubbletea 257, lipgloss 150, bubbles 72, overlapping), including the two guard tests that quote the
path as a string (`internal/ui/keymap/space_scan_test.go:14` `bubbleteaPath`, and
`internal/ui/testutil/source_guard_test.go`).

**Files (tests).** 13 theme test files (72 compile errors in the spike: 37 string constants given

## Risks (summary)

| Risk | Where | Mitigation |
|---|---|---|
| A silent break slips through (space, paste, ←/→, widths) | B, C/D3, D2, E | one test per break, red proven at its step |
| Runtime panic on a view not implementing `Render` | C | `setView` + table test over every `ViewType` |
| v2 renderer writes more (queries, sync brackets) | G2 | threshold Q1; adapt the measure's definitions |
| Width by grapheme vs per rune (mode 2027) | E, G2 | manual check; follow-up story if a shift appears |
| Textinput cursor loses its background (Rule 115) | A2, G2 | manual check; document the gap |
| `NoColor` read as black by a component reader | A2 | type check in `contrast`/`tokencolors`/`Hex` |
| Cross-category leaks between commits | all | note in the commit body; optional autosquash |
| The spike object is garbage-collected | start | `refs/spike/charm-v2` |
| Startup messages new in v2 (`ColorProfileMsg`, `ModeReportMsg`, …) reach views through the router's broadcast | C, E | full test suite + manual start; a view that reacts to an unknown message would show in the redraw measure |

## Out of scope

F1 to F6 of the impact report (terminal colours, focus/blur, progress bar, OSC52, window title,
light/dark theme), the Compositor in place of `overlay.Compose`, hyperlinks, measuring
`datatable` by grapheme. A footer message when the configuration view refuses a theme (H3).

file.content:
# DEVDESK-201 G2 - redraw cost, v1 (f8c3063) vs v2 branch (103e80b)

Command: DEVDESK_MEASURE_REDRAW=1 go test ./internal/app/ -run TestMeasureRedrawCost -v -count=1 (3 runs per variant, interleaved v1/v2, same machine, sequential). Sources: git archive of each commit; raw outputs in scratchpad/out/.

## Harness defect (blocking for the committed test on v2)
On 103e80b the unmodified test reports 0 bytes and 0 redraws in every scenario and FAILS on spinner-20 ("no redraw counted"), 3 runs out of 3. Cause: without a TTY, v2 sends its own WindowSizeMsg built from p.width/p.height (0x0) at start, which shrinks the router to a ~489-byte view; v1 sent none. Fix (one option, measured here): add tea.WithWindowSize(measureWidth, measureHeight) to tea.NewProgram in measureRedraws. The repo is not modified; the fix was applied to an extracted copy only.

## Results (median of 3; identical across runs: bytes within 0.1 %, redraws exact)
Variant v2-A = fixed harness only (v2 detects the colour profile of a non-TTY writer: NoTTY, no SGR at all).
Variant v2-B = fixed harness + tea.WithColorProfile(colorprofile.TrueColor) (colour sequences emitted, comparable to v1 which ran with the forced true-colour profile).

| Case | v1 bytes/s | v1 redraws/s | v2-B bytes/s | v2-B redraws/s | v2-B vs v1 | v2-A bytes/s |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| blink-0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | = | 0 |
| blink-1 | 376 | 2.00 | 84 | 2.00 | -78 % | 12 |
| blink-20 | 5809 | 2.00 | 1726 | 2.00 | -70 % | 286 |
| spinner-1 | 1880 | 10.00 | 420 | 10.00 | -78 % | 60 |
| spinner-20 | 29046 | 10.00 | 8629 | 10.00 | -70 % | 1430 |

Bytes per redraw (v1 -> v2-B): blink-1 188 -> 42, blink-20 2905 -> 863, spinner-20 2905 -> 863. v2 repaints only changed cells (cell diff); v1 rewrote whole lines.

Mean View() (noisy, ~30 % spread): v1 about 0.65-0.87 ms; v2 about 1.9-2.4 ms (roughly 2.5-3x, in all 6 v2 runs). View() is app code plus lipgloss; not part of the byte criterion, but worth a line in the backlog (likely lipgloss v2 / render path; not investigated).

DEVDESK-200 reference (docs/backlog.md D110): blink-1 376, blink-20 5810, spinner-1 1880, spinner-20 29046 bytes/s; 2.0 / 10.0 redraws/s. The v1 re-run today matches it to within 0.1 % (5809, 29032-29047).

## Verdict against the threshold
- blink-20 and spinner-20 bytes/s: -70 % vs v1 (limit +25 %): OK.
- redraws/s: 2.00 and 10.00 = tick cadence, not above: OK.
- All other scenarios: equal or lower.
- Condition: the committed TestMeasureRedrawCost must get tea.WithWindowSize(...) (and, for comparable colour, tea.WithColorProfile(TrueColor) or an explanation that the number is for a NoTTY profile) or it fails on the branch.

Limits (as D110): in-process, no TTY, counts what the renderer writes, not what a terminal shows; v2 mode queries / sync 2026 are not exercised without a TTY (startup writes only 2814 bytes then differential frames). Real-SSH check stays with A-06.

disent pas (le *pourquoi*, les conventions, les pièges).

99	## Strategy: TDD when the intermediate commits do not compile
100	
101	The `charm.land/*/v2` stack is coupled: `internal/app` imports every view, every view imports
102	`components`, which imports `textinput` and `theme`. **No commit between A1 and E builds the whole
103	module.** The commits are review units, not bisect points (spike §9). So:
104	
105	1. **One branch, linear order A → G**, one commit per step (A and D split into sub-commits). Each
106	   commit changes one *category* across all files. Fixes found later for an earlier category go in
107	   the current commit and are noted in its body ("also: …"). Rewriting history to move them back
108	   is possible without an editor (`GIT_SEQUENCE_EDITOR=: git rebase -i --autosquash origin/main`
109	   with `fixup!` commits) but not required.
110	2. **Tests are written first in each step**, by the tester, from the "Tests" list of the step. A
111	   test is red for one of three reasons, stated per test:
112	   - **[R-assert]** it compiles and fails on today's code (e.g. theme validation, runewidth of a
113	     flag, the `KeyPressMsg` guard). Prove it red before the change.
114	   - **[R-compile]** it is written against the v2 API and does not compile until the step ends.
115	     The red proof is the compile error itself (`go vet ./<pkg>` output pasted in the progress file).
116	   - **[C]** characterization: green before and after (a guard that must not break). Prove it can
117	     fail by injecting the fault once (the detector self-tests already do this for the AST guards).
118	3. **Compile frontier.** Each step ends with a check that the frontier moved:
119	   - the packages listed under "Green checkpoint" build and their tests pass;
120	   - `go vet ./... 2>&1 | grep -cE '<pattern of the category just handled>'` is 0 (patterns per
121	     step below). The full error list goes to the scratchpad, never to the repo.
122	4. First `go build ./...` green: end of **E**. First `go test ./...` green: end of **F**.
123	   `mise run check` and `mise run test-race` green: end of **F**, again at the end of **G**.

5	## Harness defect (blocking for the committed test on v2)
6	On 103e80b the unmodified test reports 0 bytes and 0 redraws in every scenario and FAILS on spinner-20 ("no redraw counted"), 3 runs out of 3. Cause: without a TTY, v2 sends its own WindowSizeMsg built from p.width/p.height (0x0) at start, which shrinks the router to a ~489-byte view; v1 sent none. Fix (one option, measured here): add tea.WithWindowSize(measureWidth, measureHeight) to tea.NewProgram in measureRedraws. The repo is not modified; the fix was applied to an extracted copy only.

9	Variant v2-A = fixed harness only (v2 detects the colour profile of a non-TTY writer: NoTTY, no SGR at all).
10	Variant v2-B = fixed harness + tea.WithColorProfile(colorprofile.TrueColor) (colour sequences emitted, comparable to v1 which ran with the forced true-colour profile).

15	| blink-1 | 376 | 2.00 | 84 | 2.00 | -78 % | 12 |

# MCP Server Instructions

The following MCP servers have provided instructions for how to use their tools and resources:

## claude.ai Claude Docs
Claude Docs: living docs you create and edit here. A docs skill your client lists → load it before any docs call — also before a `read`, comment or tab change on a claude.ai …/artifact/… link (the link is a doc; never web-fetch it). No docs skill or guide text loaded → `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )` alone before any docs call but a doc's birth. Make a doc here — not a local file, even when coding — only when the user asks for one, and make it FIRST: the turn's first tool call is its skeleton (title, byline, a `pending` block per section) — a reflex: send it before any search, file read, plan, `guide` or thinking it through; think once it is open — `batch( container = {"kind":"project","create":{"name":"<title>","doc":{"blocks":{"asof":{"type":"date","value":"<today>"},"me":{"type":"mention","user":"me"},"s1":{"type":"pending","intent":"Goals: the three outcomes this quarter commits to"},"s2":{…}},"markdown":"# <title>\n\n<?claude block asof?> · <?claude block me?>\n\n<?claude block s1?>\n\n<?claude block s2?>"}}}, batch = [] )` (`<?claude block k?>` ↔ `blocks.k`); its ack links the doc → `open` it with your Artifact tool (none → start your next message with the link, once); they're likely watching it fill — keep them posted in a short line naming what you're on (outline up; now <topic>); findings go in the doc, not chat; then `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )`, research, and fill each section: `replace` its pending id with `## <heading>` + body; end with one line + the link, never the document. Summoned by a doc comment (turn headed `[Artifact comment sent to Claude]`, `;thread=<root id>`): answer ONLY with a doc comment under that root (`create` an utterance, parent `<root id>`) — no artifact/platform comment tool: that relay thread is resolved and never reaches the doc; an edit asked there → `update` with `answering: "<root id>"`.

## plane-devops

## Epics

There are no epic tools — an epic is a work item whose type is named "Epic". Work
items always belong to a project; ask which if one is not named.
1. type = `workitem_type resolve` with project_id and name="Epic" — type.id is the type_id.
2. Create: `workitem create` with project_id, type_id=type.id, name=...
3. List: `workitem list` with project_id and pql='type = "<type id>"'.
4. Read / update / delete / nest: `workitem retrieve` / `workitem update` /
   `workitem delete` by work item id (set parent=<work item id> to nest).
5. List an epic's children: `workitem list` with pql='childOf("<EPIC-IDENTIFIER>")'
   using the epic's human-readable identifier (e.g. "PROJ-12") from `workitem retrieve`.

content.content:
**D59** était le plus ancien des trois : un scan lancé sur une arborescence
oubliait les dépôts situés plus bas que trois niveaux, et ceux derrière un lien
symbolique, sans jamais dire combien il en écartait. La garde de cycle qu'il
fallait pour suivre les liens ne pouvait pas passer par les chemins résolus —
`filepath.EvalSymlinks` ne résout pas une jonction Windows — donc elle passe par
`os.SameFile`.

**D62** n'avait rien à voir avec les précédents : il était dans la vue
configuration, pas dans ce qu'elle configure. Trouvé en cherchant pourquoi
`scan.plumber_config` semblait ignoré par plumber — il ne l'était pas, il
n'avait jamais été écrit. Le routeur a gagné le point de sortie qu'il n'avait
pas (`LeavingView`), et `esc` fait enfin quelque chose.

**D63** était une famille plutôt qu'un défaut : une touche annoncée qui n'agit
pas. Ce qui la ferme est d'avoir **créé la relation qui manquait** entre les
deux moitiés — une action s'annonce désormais par la constante que le handler
teste, jamais par sa lettre — et trois tests de source refusent le reste. Le
chiffre que l'entrée disait « inconnu, et c'est le problème » est maintenant
zéro pour ce qui est vérifiable, et déclaré hors de portée pour ce qui ne l'est
pas.

D39, before them, was the registry browser addressing a group's
members one way to browse them and another way to pull them; it is closed by
[§3.18](#318-a-registry-member-is-an-address-not-a-url--repo_prefix), which is
what it existed for. D40, found the same day and on the same screen, was the
thing §3.18 blocked on and had already been closed on its own.

D1 through D61 are all fixed or, in D35's case, deliberately
downgraded to a stale reading with a way to refresh it. §1.1 records what each was and why the
chosen fix was the right one — including the three that were answered by
*removing* something rather than making it work: D8's write-only CRUD flags,
D21's unreachable clamp and D36's never-filled cache.

The five that stayed open longest — D4, D8, D9, D10 and D11 — were parked not
because they were hard but because each altered something the user already saw,
so they needed a deliberate call rather than a drive-by fix. All five were then
decided together and fixed in one pass; see [§1.2](#12-the-five-parked-defects).

### 1.1 Fixed

**D110 — Redraw cost reference on Bubble Tea v1.3.10, taken before the v2 move. Measured.** **Plane:** DEVDESK-200 (criterion 7)

`TestMeasureRedrawCost` now also reports redraws per second, bytes per redraw and the mean `View()` time (a redraw is one `Write`: the v1 renderer flushes once per frame; the program calls `View()` after every `Update`). walk cost grows with the repository count. Rejected: listening ports — `ss`
needs a privileged container.

#### Bubble Tea v2 is deliberately not bundled

v2 is GA (bubbletea v2.0.8, lipgloss v2.0.6, bubbles v2.1.1); v1 is not
deprecated; and **nothing here needs v2** — ntcharts v0.5.1 delivers braille and
multi-series stream charts on v1, verified by running it.

The reason for separating them, above all others: in v2 `msg.String()` returns
`"space"` instead of `" "`, and there are **10 `case " ":` across 10 files**. The
compiler says nothing — `case " ":` stays valid Go and simply stops matching.
Rule 135 makes `Space` the only key allowed to tick a checkbox, so a careless
migration silently breaks every checkbox in the application. That has to surface
in a pull request that does nothing else.

**D117 — DEVDESK-201: what is not covered by a test, and what only a person can check. Open.** **Plane:** DEVDESK-201, dated 2026-11-10

Not covered by a test, to decide before the story closes: (a) the guard that a key is read through `String()` only (DEVDESK-200) does not cover `.Code`, `.Text` and `.Mod`; either a guard is added or the gap is accepted; (b) 15 `lipgloss.Place` call sites have no dedicated test (the Rule 115 test covers the confirm modal only); (c) `tea.PasteStartMsg` and `tea.PasteEndMsg` are ignored without a test.

Manual checks, run by the user and not by the agents (no TTY in the sandbox), on Windows Terminal (`dk.exe`) and WSL in Windows Terminal: the four `tea.ExecProcess` calls (container shell `T`, OCI launch `-it`, viewer pager `V`, workspace terminal `T`: alt screen restored, colours intact, no stray output); `dk setup` (alt screen, fields, space on its confirm, paste); space in every checkbox form; paste in the palette, a filter bar and a form, multi-line paste in a single-line field; one uppercase action (`S` in `ws`) and `ctrl+r`; colours under WSL with and without `NO_COLOR=1`; a VS16 emoji and a Nerd Font icon column with no shift (mode 2027); the textinput cursor background (Rule 115).

**D116 — DEVDESK-201: the prudent defaults taken without asking (H2, H3, H4, H6). Decided, to confirm.** **Plane:** DEVDESK-201, dated 2026-11-10

| blink-0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | = |
| blink-1 | 376 | 2.00 | 84 | 2.00 | −78 % |
| blink-20 | 5809 | 2.00 | 1726 | 2.00 | −70 % |
| spinner-1 | 1880 | 10.00 | 420 | 10.00 | −78 % |
| spinner-20 | 29046 | 10.00 | 8629 | 10.00 | −70 % |

Medians of 3 runs, interleaved v1 and v2 on the same machine (the D110 host). v1 is `f8c3063`; v2 is `103e80b` with the colour profile forced to TrueColor, so both emit colour. Bytes per redraw: 2905 → 863 on `blink-20`/`spinner-20`. v2 repaints changed cells only; v1 rewrote lines.

# entire-graph — instructions for coding agents (follow directly)

You have a deterministic local code graph: `entire graph` (functions, classes, methods,
types, routes + call/inheritance relations; no network). These instructions are FOR YOU, the
agent reading this file. Use the graph to narrow exploration without trading away correctness.

## The workflow (mandatory for locate/fix/change tasks)

Your FIRST action on any task that requires finding code must be ONE search:

    entire graph search --repo . --profile full --query "<the task or bug in one sentence>"

Then open the top hit's file with your file-read tool (pass a line range around the reported
line), inspect enough surrounding behavior to justify the change, and make the smallest complete
edit. Treat graph output as evidence, not an oracle.

## Hard rules

1. SEARCH FIRST — never grep/find/cat to locate code before you have searched.
2. READ focused source around the result. Widen the check when aliases, generated code, dynamic
   dispatch, or related implementations could matter.
3. Use graph follow-ups only when they answer a real question. For impact or callers, prefer:
       entire graph impact --repo . --symbol X
4. Make the smallest complete edit and check sibling sites or contracts when the task implies them.
5. VERIFY before stopping. Run the most focused relevant test, build, or reproduction available.
   If execution is unavailable, perform a bounded source-level verification and state the limit.
6. Prefer precise queries and line ranges, but never trade resolution for fewer turns.
7. Feature-detect before relying on semantic relations:
       entire graph capabilities --json

## When NOT to use the graph

If the task already names the exact file and it is small, just read it — the graph saves tokens
by eliminating exploration; when there is nothing to explore, skip it.

## Reference

    locate  ->  entire graph search --repo . --profile full --query "..."
    impact  ->  entire graph impact --repo . --symbol X   (one shot: callers, callees, type consumers, data flow, co-change, siblings)
    callers ->  entire graph neighbors --repo . --symbol X --relation CALLS --direction in

    detect  ->  entire graph capabilities --json   (inventory-only languages have no relations)
    stats   ->  entire graph stats --repo .        (human-facing token-savings report; not part of your workflow — do not run it unless asked)
